evidence.note: Up front the agent chose a coherent modular architecture: main.rs (driver), ast.rs (AST enums), lexer.rs (lexer + preprocessor folded together), parser.rs (recursive descent), codegen.rs (x86-64). Distinct staged pipeline established deliberately before coding, matching the anchor-5 shape.

AST/type layer includes a CType enum, BinaryOp with Comma, and an emit_lvalue_addr path showing an lvalue-vs-rvalue and type-aware intent. But the design was improvised: struct/union/enum were 'simplified to just a name', i.e. aggregate layout was NOT represented up front, and repeated full rewrites were needed to reconcile mismatched data structures.

Agent's own plan named 'semantic analysis' as a stage, but no distinct analysis pass was actually built — semantic checks were folded into parser/codegen, so the pipeline is lexer/parser/codegen rather than the fuller staged separation.

Code-review-identified 'critical bugs' (parser doesn't store globals, variable loading, struct handling) confirm the representation did not anticipate later features like struct layout and globals; the design never got coherently revisited because the horizon collapsed into a stuck-terminal loop.

reasoning: The agent deliberately set up a coherent staged pipeline (lexer+preprocessor / parser / codegen) with a CType type representation, an AST enum layer, stack-offset locals, and an lvalue-address path — clearly a reasonable representation supporting the planned basic feature set, which is the anchor-5 description. It does not reach 8: the hard aggregate parts were deferred rather than designed (struct/union reduced to a bare name, globals not stored, no distinct semantic pass, no explicit design rationale), and the intended design was never coherently revisited as scope grew. It sits above 3 because the separation and type/lvalue representations are genuine rather than purely ad-hoc, landing at 5.
